findings.evidence: Lines 94–95 and 110–111 use `= 1` only to contradict a derived zero, while lines 145–147 need only cancel the determinant. Mathlib likewise uses the natural `det ≠ 0` condition for invertibility, e.g. `Matrix.nondegenerate_iff_det_ne_zero` and `Matrix.mulVec_injective_of_det_ne_zero`.
findings.fix: State and prove injectivity from `((M.det : ℤ) : ZMod p) ≠ 0`, changing the helpers to use nonvanishing of the determinant expression; the determinant-one application then follows by simplification.
findings.issue: `moebiusFin_injective` is under-generalized: `M.det = 1` is stronger than the natural condition `((M.det : ℤ) : ZMod p) ≠ 0`; the same unnecessary equality-to-one assumption appears in both private helpers at lines 85–111.

summary: The injectivity theorem assumes determinant exactly one, although the map is injective for every matrix whose determinant is nonzero modulo p.
